title: Regularity of the parameter blowup algebra
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d\geq1$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ be a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and $j\in J$. Write $L=J\setminus\{j\}$ and set $$A=R[u_i\mid i\in L]/(t_i-t_j u_i\mid i\in L).$$ Coefficients and variables in quotient rings are denoted by the same symbols. Then $A$ is a Noetherian regular ring. There are canonical isomorphisms $$A/(t_j)\cong (R/(t_i:i\in J))[u_i\mid i\in L],\qquad A[1/t_j]\cong R[1/t_j],$$ where the latter sends $u_i$ to $t_i/t_j$. Multiplication by $t_j$ on $A$ is injective. In particular, for every prime ideal $P\subset A$, the local ring $A_P$ is regular local, whether or not $t_j\in P$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121: regularity of the standard parameter chart, its exceptional quotient and its complement

proof.text: Order $J$ with $j$ first and extend it to an ordering of all $d$ parameters. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], this reordered full list is regular, its prefix $(t_j,(t_i)_{i\in L})$ is regular, and $C=R/(t_i:i\in J)$ is regular local of dimension $d-|J|$. For the prefix, injectivity is part of the full-list condition, and its quotient is nonzero since it surjects onto the nonzero quotient by the full list. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], both $R$ and $C$ are regular rings.

Put $B=R[u_i\mid i\in L]$ and $H=(t_i-t_ju_i\mid i\in L)$, so $A=B/H$. By [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base], $B$ is regular, hence Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] to $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ to see that $A$ is Noetherian. The same polynomial lemma applied to the regular ring $C$ of Step 1 shows that $C[u_i\mid i\in L]$ is regular.

source.place: Tags 00OQ (polynomial regularity) and 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); polynomial regularity is the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The canonical map $B\to C[u_i\mid i\in L]$ kills $H$ and $t_j$. Conversely $R\to A/(t_j)$ kills every $t_i$ for $i\in J$, since $t_i=t_ju_i$ in $A$. It induces $C\to A/(t_j)$, which extends to a polynomial map sending each variable to its class. These maps are inverse: their composites fix coefficients and all variables, which generate the rings, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus $A/(t_j)\cong C[u_i\mid i\in L]$. Also evaluation $u_i\mapsto t_i/t_j$ kills $H$ and induces $\alpha:A[1/t_j]\to R[1/t_j]$. The coefficient map induces $\beta:R[1/t_j]\to A[1/t_j]$. The composites fix $R$ and $t_j^{-1}$, and $\beta\alpha(u_i)=t_i t_j^{-1}=u_i$ by the defining relation. These elements generate the respective localizations, so $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are inverse. Both isomorphisms have the asserted coefficient and variable images.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121: explicit coordinate substitutions; expanded elementary quotient and localization computation.

proof.text: Set $I=(t_i:i\in J)$. Apply [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] to the regular prefix from Step 1, with $a=t_j$ and remaining entries $(t_i)_{i\in L}$. Changing the signs of the defining relations changes no ideal, so it identifies $A$ with $R[I/t_j]$, sending $u_i$ to $t_i/t_j$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] this is a subalgebra of $R[1/t_j]$. If $t_jx=0$ in $A$, its image in that localization is zero after cancellation of the unit $t_j$; the injectivity of the subalgebra inclusion then gives $x=0$. This proves the required injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence), quotient presentation and torsion-free conclusion.

proof.text: Fix a prime $P\subset A$ with $t_j\in P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $A_P$ is Noetherian. Step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime], with the one-element list $(t_j)$, show that $(t_j/1)$ is regular in $A_P$. In particular it lies in the maximal ideal. Let $\bar P=P/(t_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $A_P/(t_j/1)\cong (A/(t_j))_{\bar P}$. Steps 2 and 3 identify this with a localization at a prime of the regular ring $C[u_i]$, so it is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. All hypotheses of [lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient] now hold for the Noetherian local ring $A_P$ and its one-element regular sequence; hence $A_P$ is regular local.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), 00NU (lemma-regular-mod-x); regular-sequence localization is the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Now suppose $t_j\notin P$. The powers of $t_j$ belong to $A\setminus P$. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] with $M=\{t_j^n:n\ge0\}$ and $N=A\setminus P$. It says that the induced map $A[1/t_j]\to A_P$ is a localization at the image of $N$. Step 3 identifies its source with $R[1/t_j]$. Since $R$ is regular by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] first gives regularity of $R[1/t_j]$, then of $A_P$. This is a local ring; its localization at its maximal ideal is itself, since all elements outside that ideal are already units. Thus the definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] gives that $A_P$ is regular local. Steps 5 and 6 cover every prime; together with the Noetherianity in Step 2 they prove that $A$ is a regular ring. The two canonical isomorphisms are Step 3, and injectivity is Step 4.

source.place: Tags 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), 00OD (definition-regular), and 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular), proof Step 3: localization of a regular ring.

Step 3: I checked both explicit inverse pairs, A/(t_j)≅C[u] and A[1/t_j]≅R[1/t_j] (βα(u_i)=t_j u_i t_j^{-1}=u_i); marking it elementary is acceptable. Step 5 (t_j∈P): t_j/1 is regular in A_P, the quotient A_P/(t_j) is regular local, so the lift lemma makes A_P regular local; all hypotheses hold. Step 6 (t_j∉P): A_P is a localization of R[1/t_j], hence regular. Edge cases J={j}, d=1 and J=all indices (C a field) all work. lean.statement: theorem parameterBlowupAlgebra_regular {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (t : Fin d → R) (ht : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn t)) (J : Finset (Fin d)) (hJ : J.Nonempty) (j : Fin d) (hj : j ∈ J) : IsNoetherianRing (traceChartRing t J j) ∧ IsRegularRing (traceChartRing t J j) ∧ (∃ e : (traceChartRing t J j ⧸ Ideal.span ({algebraMap R (traceChartRing t J j) (t j)} : Set (traceChartRing t J j))) ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial (J.erase j) (R ⧸ Ideal.span (t '' (J : Set (Fin d)))), ∀ i : J.erase j, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (traceChartCoordinate t J j i.val i.property)) = MvPolynomial.X i) ∧ (∃ e : Localization.Away (algebraMap R (traceChartRing t J j) (t j)) ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away (t j), ∀ i : J.erase j, e (algebraMap (traceChartRing t J j) _ (traceChartCoordinate t J j i.val i.property)) = algebraMap R (Localization.Away (t j)) (t i.val) * IsLocalization.Away.invSelf (t j)) ∧ Function.Injective (fun x : traceChartRing t J j ↦ algebraMap R (traceChartRing t J j) (t j) * x) ∧ (∀ (P : Ideal (traceChartRing t J j)) [P.IsPrime], IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime P))
